synthesis: Restricting the Λ-real foliation to its even-indexed Gram family, Λ and Φ recover the same critical-line phase sections while supplying different off-axis coordinates: the Λ contours are asymptotically horizontal and carry a monotone signed magnitude, whereas the Φ-real contours pass through the same Gram points with asymptotic slope -π/(2 log t).
source_support: The definitions give Λ(s)=Φ(1-s)/Φ(s) and identify Gram ordinates as critical-line phase sections. Lemmas 2 and 3 make even-indexed real-Λ contours cross the critical line at Gram points and place them within O(1/t) of horizontal intervals; Lemma 4 makes Re Λ strictly monotone on those contours for sufficiently large t. Lemma 7 independently makes real-Φ contours cross at Gram points but with asymptotic slope -π/(2 log t) and O(1/t) displacement from the corresponding tilted intervals.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis aligns two equivalent functional-equation multipliers by their shared Gram crossings, then contrasts what each representation exposes away from the critical line: Λ separates phase selection from monotone amplitude, while Φ changes the contour direction. That shared-crossing/different-coordinate comparison requires the contour geometry and monotonicity parents jointly.
limits: Only the even-indexed Λ contours are the shared Gram family; odd-indexed Λ contours cross where ζ is imaginary. All geometric and monotonicity statements are asymptotic, the latter requires sufficiently large t, and exact coefficients and remainders are formula-sensitive. The comparison neither locates or controls zeta zeros nor proves positivity on Gram lines.
quality_reason: Accepted because distinct parent units establish both an invariant crossing set and a concrete representation-dependent change in contour geometry, with Λ's monotone magnitude adding information absent from the Φ account. The synthesis narrows the candidate to the even-indexed Gram family and preserves the source's asymptotic and OCR limits.

synthesis: The mean estimate is assembled as a transport chain: curvature of the continuously indexed Gram phase yields a uniform cosine-sum cancellation bound; the direct and functional-equation-dual sums are reduced to those oscillations; reordering and partial summation preserve the cancellation under moving truncations and weights; and a σ-dependent transition balances this low-σ analysis against the Dirichlet-series regime to obtain a bound uniform for σ>0.
source_support: Lemma 8 differentiates the inverse Gram-phase parametrization twice and applies a second-derivative estimate to obtain an absolute O(N^(1/2) log N) cosine-sum bound. The high-σ part applies that bound to the Dirichlet series. For 0<σ<σ_N, the approximate functional equation and Λ asymptotics at Gram ordinates produce the deterministic 1 plus power correction and the two oscillatory terms F1 and F2. The proof then reverses the moving summation region for F1 and uses partial summation for weighted F2 before choosing σ_N by minimizing an error envelope and combining both σ regimes.
nonparaphrase_operation: This composes several parents into an estimate-transport mechanism: phase curvature creates cancellation in the Gram index, the approximate functional equation exposes that same cancellative kernel in two differently weighted representations, and optimization chooses the seam at which their error bounds hand off to the high-σ representation. No single parent contains this full dependency chain.
limits: The theorem is asymptotic in N and covers only σ>0; it gives an aggregate corrected-mean error, not pointwise control of ζ. The plotted 5120-point agreement is numerical evidence rather than a proof. Exact powers, logarithmic factors, truncation limits, and the minimizing formula are extraction-sensitive and require the retained source image before symbol-level reuse.
quality_reason: Accepted because the parents explicitly support every link from Gram-phase curvature through cancellation, two-sided approximate-functional-equation decomposition, weighted estimate transfer, and σ-regime balancing. The synthesis is a proof-architecture relation rather than a thematic summary and retains the open-half-plane and transcription boundaries.

synthesis: The corrected mean supplies a rigorous but strictly weaker positivity signal for the motivating zero-count criterion: for each fixed 0<σ<1 it forces infinitely many sampled values Re ζ(σ+i g_n)>0, while the argument-principle reduction requires Re ζ>0 at every point of an entire horizontal boundary segment at a Gram height to make the zero count a nearest-integer value.
source_support: The motivation unit shows that positivity of Re ζ on the whole top segment C makes log ζ single-valued there, confines the logarithmic-derivative contribution to (-1/2,1/2), and hence fixes N(T) as the nearest integer to θ(T)/π+1; the authors identify infinitely many Gram heights with this property as an objective. The final corollaries derive an eventual positive linear lower bound for the sampled sum and conclude that, for each fixed 0<σ<1, infinitely many Gram ordinates have positive real part.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis compares the quantifiers and geometric domains of two positivity statements: aggregate control implies recurring positivity at isolated samples, whereas winding-number rigidity needs pathwise right-half-plane containment. Relating the average-to-existence mechanism to the branch-of-logarithm mechanism exposes exactly why the proved result is evidence for, but cannot discharge, the motivating proof burden.
limits: Positive values at isolated Gram ordinates, even infinitely often and on each fixed line in the proved strip, do not imply positivity along the full boundary interval or at one common Gram height across all σ on that interval. The source does not prove the desired infinite nearest-integer zero-count family, and extension to σ=0 or farther left is conjectural. Integral and exponent typography remains OCR-sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted because the two parents jointly support a concrete implication gap rather than a generic positivity theme: one turns full-segment positivity into zero-count rigidity, while the other turns a mean bound only into infinitely many positive point samples. The synthesis preserves the source's own evidence language and makes the missing pathwise uniformity explicit.
